title: Clover’s RSV-hMPV Vaccine Shows Antibody Rises in Phase 2 Trial - The Clinical Trial Vanguard

analysis.time: The Phase 2 trial data was released on September 6, 2026, and the study was conducted on adults aged 60 to 85 in Australia. The publication date is September 7, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The trial was conducted in Australia, involving 420 adults aged 60 to 85. The target population is adults aged 60 to 85, with a focus on those 75 and older who may have pre-existing immunity.
analysis.event: Clover’s Phase 2 trial of its RSV-hMPV vaccine candidates (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) showed significant neutralizing antibody rises against both RSV and hMPV. The trial also found no immune interference when PIV3 antigen was added. These results were reported by The Clinical Trial Vanguard.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The trial demonstrated 6-to-9-fold neutralizing antibody rises against RSV and 6-to-8-fold rises against hMPV at 28 days post-vaccination. There were no serious adverse events, no events of special interest, and no discontinuations. The study also noted a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections in vaccinated participants, though this was based on adverse event reporting rather than PCR confirmation.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Clover plans to evaluate mid- and late-stage development plans and seek global partnership opportunities. The company has completed commercial-scale bioreactor production of all three antigen components, which reduces late-stage manufacturing risks. However, the Phase 3 trial plans and funding readiness are still under consideration.

analysis.brief_en: Clover’s Phase 2 trial of its RSV-hMPV vaccine candidates, SCB-1022 and SCB-1033, showed significant neutralizing antibody rises against both RSV and hMPV in 420 adults aged 60 to 85 in Australia. The study, published on September 7, 2026, found no immune interference when PIV3 antigen was added, suggesting the vaccine could offer broader protection for those with pre-existing immunity. Safety data indicated no serious adverse events, with most solicited adverse events being mild and resolving within two days. The trial also noted a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections in vaccinated participants, though this was based on adverse event reporting rather than PCR confirmation. Clover plans to evaluate mid- and late-stage development and seek global partnerships, but no Phase 3 start date has been announced. The company has completed commercial-scale production of all three antigen components, reducing manufacturing risks. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require further outcomes-based validation in Phase 3 trials.

analysis.event: Clover announced positive Phase 2 clinical data for RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 respiratory combination vaccine candidates in older adults. The study was a randomized, observer-blinded, multi-center trial with 420 participants.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The vaccine groups (SCB-1022 and SCB-1033) showed approximately 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections compared to the placebo group within 28 days of vaccination. analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is ongoing and the results are preliminary. No PCR sequencing was conducted to confirm infection cases, and the findings are based on adverse event reporting. The trial is part of Clover's development of multi-valent protein-based respiratory vaccines.

analysis.brief_en: Clover has announced positive Phase 2 clinical data for its RSV + hMPV ± PIV3 respiratory combination vaccine candidates in older adults. The trial, conducted in Australia with 420 participants aged 60-85, was a randomized, observer-blinded, multi-center study. Results showed a 62% lower rate of respiratory tract infections in the vaccine groups compared to the placebo group within 28 days of vaccination, based on adverse event reporting. Neutralizing antibody responses were observed, with fold rises of 6-9 for RSV, 6-8 for hMPV, and greater than 3 for PIV3. The findings are preliminary, as no PCR sequencing was performed to confirm infection cases. The study validates Clover's Trimer-Tag platform for developing multi-valent protein-based respiratory vaccines, which could impact public health and chronic diseases caused by respiratory viruses. The results are part of ongoing research and do not yet indicate the vaccine's full efficacy or safety profile.
